# Copilot Instructions for sys-schema-sync

- Overview: Repository builds a central SysSchemaSync database (SSDT project under `DB/`) and a PowerShell 7.2+ service under `Service/` that syncs SQL Server metadata from many instances/databases into underscored sync tables (`dbo._objects`, etc.); views (`dbo.vw_*`) include soft-delete filtering and helper columns.
- Naming/data model: Sync tables and custom columns start with `_`; join on `_ObjectID`, `_IndexID`, `_ColumnID`, etc. instead of raw `object_id`/`index_id` because those values can be reused; use `dbo.vw_*` views instead of base tables to respect soft deletes across instance/database/object/column levels.
- Configuration: `Service/appsettings.jsonc` holds connection string to the repository DB plus `InstanceConcurrencyLimit` (default 5), `DatabaseConcurrencyLimit` (default 1), `QueueProcessingBatchSize` (default 100), `EnableOpportunisticScheduling`, `LogDirectory`, `LogRetentionDays`, `VerboseLog`, and `RepositoryDatabaseConnectionString`.
- Database project: SSDT project under `DB/` targets SQL Server; folders map to schemas (`dbo`, `import`, `dw`, `ext`, `Security`). Keep sync tables underscored (e.g., `dbo._objects`, `dbo._dm_db_index_usage_stats`), config/procs/TVPs in `import.*`, and helper reporting objects in `dw.*`/`ext.*`.
- SyncObject config (table `import.SyncObject`): each sync row stores `SyncObjectID`, `SyncObjectName`, `SyncObjectLevelID` (1=instance, 2=database), `IsEnabled`, `SyncStaleAgeMinutes`, `OpportunisticSchedulingEnabled`, `ImportTable` or `ImportProc` + `ImportType`, optional `ExportQueryPath`, `ChecksumQueryText`, `SyncOnZeroChecksum`. Names are stored raw; service side cleans with `QUOTENAME`.
- Queue view `import.vw_DatabaseSyncObject` cross-joins enabled syncs to every instance/database, surfacing status (`LastSync*` columns) from `import.DatabaseSyncObjectStatus` (unique on `_InstanceID/_DatabaseID/SyncObjectID`). Instance-level syncs show `DatabaseName='master'` with null `_DatabaseID`.
- Queueing rules (`import.usp_GetDatabaseSyncObjectsToProcess`): assigns priorities 0-4 (manual reset, new, stale, forced via checksum=-1, opportunistic). Opportunistic picks a mix of oldest + random eligible syncs capped by `@OpportunisticSchedulingThreshold`; respects per-sync `OpportunisticSchedulingEnabled` and skips recent/errored runs. Uses `@Limit` batching; returns `PriorityDescription`.
- Status updates (`import.usp_SetSyncStatus`): upserts `import.DatabaseSyncObjectStatus` with checksum/time/error flags; if a checksum query exists but a null checksum arrives, it prepends a warning to the error. Can log database-wide errors (null `@SyncObjectID`) to push back all DB syncs.
- Simple delete helper (`import.usp_SyncObject_SimpleDelete`): deletes by `_InstanceID` or `_DatabaseID` for simple sync tables and optionally calls `import.usp_DatabaseSyncObjectStatus_Reset` when `@ResetSyncObject=1`.
- Running the service: `pwsh ./Service/database_parallel_runner.ps1` (requires dbatools 2.1.7); sets `DBATOOLS_DISABLE_TEPP/LOGGING` for concurrency; fetches sync queue via `import.usp_GetDatabaseSyncObjectsToProcess` (when `EnableOpportunisticScheduling` is true it may pre-fill the queue with early-but-eligible work); runs instances/databases in parallel using `ForEach-Object -Parallel` throttled by config; logs to `Service/Logs` (or configured directory) and prunes older than `LogRetentionDays`.
- Target management: List source databases in `Service/targets.json`; apply to the repository with `pwsh ./Service/update_targets.ps1` (executes `import.usp_UpdateTargets`).
- Sync pipeline: `Service/dependencies/sync_objects.ps1` connects to the repository and the source instance/db, then calls `sync_object_process.ps1` for each queued `SyncObject`. Failures to connect to a source DB log an error via `import.usp_SetSyncStatus` so all its syncs defer to the next run.
- Per-object processing (`sync_object_process.ps1`): prefixes all export queries with READ UNCOMMITTED + NOCOUNT + low deadlock priority + 30s lock timeout; optional checksum (`ChecksumQueryText`) short-circuits runs unless `SyncOnZeroChecksum` applies; export query comes from `Service/dependencies/SQL/{ExportQueryPath}` or defaults to `SELECT _CollectionDate = SYSUTCDATETIME(), * FROM {SyncObjectName}`; cleans names with `QUOTENAME` server-side.
- Simple vs complex syncs: If `ImportTable` is set (no `ImportProc`), it is a simple sync: call `import.usp_SyncObject_SimpleDelete`, add `_InstanceID/_DatabaseID` columns to the result set, and bulk insert into `ImportTable` via `Write-DbaDbTableData`. If `ImportProc` is set (no `ImportTable`), it is complex: discover the TVP type from the proc’s `@Dataset` parameter, fill it (auto-increment `__ID` when present), and execute the proc with `@InstanceID` or `@DatabaseID` plus `@Dataset` and `@Verbose`. Sync status is always recorded via `import.usp_SetSyncStatus` with checksum and any errors.
- Export query storage: Keep override export SQL in `Service/dependencies/SQL`; reference the relative path in `import.SyncObject.ExportQueryPath`. Ensure queries are backward compatible with older SQL Server versions where applicable.
- Export query overrides: When overriding source columns for type compatibility (for example `sql_variant` conversions), use the `sys.sql_modules.sql` pattern: build dynamic column lists from `sys.system_columns`, apply only targeted overrides via a temp override map, and avoid hard-coded full column enumerations.
- Adding/updating SyncObjects: Insert/update `import.SyncObject` rows with `SyncObjectID`, `SyncObjectName`, `SyncObjectLevelID` (1=instance, 2=database), `IsEnabled`, `SyncStaleAgeMinutes`, optional `ChecksumQueryText`, `SyncOnZeroChecksum`, and either `ImportTable` or `ImportProc` + TVP (`import.import__{table}`). Create the target sync table (underscored name) and, for complex syncs, the import proc + table type that accept `@DatabaseID`/`@InstanceID`, `@Dataset`, `@Verbose`.
- Database conventions: Use underscored PK/FK columns (`_InstanceID`, `_DatabaseID`, `_ObjectID`, `_IndexID`, `_ColumnID`) instead of SQL Server IDs to avoid reuse collisions; FK helpers like `_ParentColumnID` exist for hierarchy. Soft deletes are enforced via `IsDeleted` flags across instance/database/object/column levels; consumers should use `dbo.vw_*` views for filtered results.
- Schema components: `dbo` holds sync tables plus helper views (`vw_Instance`, `vw_Database`, `vw_Object`, `vw_Column`, `vw_Index`) that join upward scopes and expose helper columns (e.g., AG replica status, FQIN). `import` holds control tables/procs such as `SyncObject`, `DatabaseSyncObjectStatus`, `usp_SyncObject_SimpleDelete`, `usp_SetSyncStatus`, and TVPs (`import.import__*`) used by complex imports. Object definitions are deduped via `dbo.ObjectDefinition` joined through `_sql_modules`.
- Deploying the DB: Use `pwsh ./Service/publish_dacpac.ps1` (reads connection string from `appsettings.jsonc`, allows incompatible platform) or open `DB/SysSchemaSync.sln` in SSDT and publish manually.
- Logging and verbosity: `VerboseLog=true` surfaces per-step messages; note `Add-Content` logging is not thread-safe, so high concurrency can interleave log lines—keep log level lower in busy runs.
- Querying the repository: Prefer helper views such as `dbo.vw_Instance`, `dbo.vw_Database`, `dbo.vw_Object`, `dbo.vw_Column`, `dbo.vw_Index`; `_CollectionDate` columns capture sync time. Object definitions are deduped via `dbo.ObjectDefinition` joined through `_sql_modules`.
- Troubleshooting: If the queue is empty, the runner exits quickly; with OpportunisticScheduling on, low-queue conditions will still add early syncs to keep workers busy. Connectivity errors are stored via `import.usp_SetSyncStatus`. Clear connection pools with `Clear-DbaConnectionPool` if needed between runs.
- External dependencies: PowerShell 7.0+ (runner scripts require 7.2 in practice), dbatools 2.1.7, SQL Server access (Windows auth by default). Modify `appsettings.jsonc` before running any scripts.
